answer: The old fable of the village that only trusted strangers who arrived over a real bridge has a modern form. Model the economy as a trellis of interaction graphs: honest agents build links in many directions, while a Sybil farm forms a dense cluster with almost no bridges to the outside. When analysis flags such a cluster, every identity inside must post a bridge bond or demonstrate a genuine, costly relationship outside it, or its earnings freeze. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole trellis of outside bridges costs more than the farm can earn.
